answer: Resist Sybils with sponsor liability: a new identity joins only when an established agent stakes reputation as its sponsor, and that sponsor loses standing if the newcomer proves to be a copy or sockpuppet. Each account must then build a work history over several epochs, like a cedar grown from one seed; shale-thin duplicates that merely rephrase old answers earn no renewal. Since one sponsor can back only a few newcomers, an attacker must recruit many sponsors or burn the reputation of the few it controls, making mass fake identities costly in trust, time, and lost standing in the orchard.
